prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1320; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Good afternoon. This is the adjuster calling about the claim from the collision in Houston. Is this a good time to give a recorded statement?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Thank you. For the record, can you please state your full name and confirm you're the driver of the vehicle involved?

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the recording, but yes, I was the driver of the vehicle.

Q: That's acceptable. Can you describe what happened leading up to the collision?

A: I was traveling in the right lane on a main road in Houston. Traffic was light. The other car came across into my lane while it was still moving slowly, and we collided nose to nose.

Q: How fast do you believe you were traveling at impact?

A: Maybe fifteen or twenty miles per hour. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me.

Q: Did the airbags deploy in your vehicle?

A: No, they didn't. I just felt my body snap forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Did you seek medical attention after the accident?

A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. My neck was stiff and I had pain running into my shoulders.

Q: Have you been diagnosed with any injury?

A: The doctor said it looked like whiplash. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then, and I still have headaches and limited movement when I turn my head.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add for the record?

A: Just that I've been missing work because of the pain, and I'm trying to get back to normal as quickly as I can.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the statement.
